To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the worst case performance of optical transmission is not necessarily obtained for a fixed PMD value but for the maximum PMD value of the link, which is a function of distance.
the PMD-induced penalty is a function of the number of spans and the span length, but not of the number of channels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following issues: (i) the statistical distribution of the PMD-induced pulse broadening and (ii) the influence of the pulse broadening on the bit-error-rate of optical transmission systems.

the following topics: 1) the development of a worst-case model for PMD in optical fibers; 2) the development of worst case simulation techniques for optical transmission systems; and 3) the application of the worst case simulation to the design of optical transmission systems.
the development and application of a new simulation technique to the study of the impact of PMD on the performance of high-speed optical transmission systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the method presented is a very useful tool in assessing the worst-case performance for optical transmission systems.
the worst-case performance is not necessarily the worst case for all channels.

the worst-case simulation method presented here is a powerful tool to estimate the non-regenerated reach of long-haul WDM systems subject to PM-D, and that the results of this method compare very well with the results obtained by a full simulation of the optical transmission system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the worst-case performance for a given PMD parameter is obtained for a given input polarisation state that is orthogonal to the instantaneous eigenstate of the PMD operator at the receiver.

the PMD induced performance degradation of long-haul optical links is dominated by the PMD-induced pulse broadening and the corresponding reduction of signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) due to the increase in ASE noise bandwidth.
the worst-case PMD-induced penalty is given by the product of the PMD-induced pulse broadening with the pulse bandwidth.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the worst case performance is determined by a combination of the PMD and the ASE noise of the transmission link.
, for a given fiber type, PMD-induced penalties are mainly determined by the channel spacing.
PMD is an important impairment in high-speed optical systems and that it is important to include PMD in system simulations.
